greetSimpler.hi: Aaj hum bhinn ko ek seedhi rekha par jagah denge.
greetSimpler.en: Today we give fractions their place on a straight line.

asidePark.hi: Yeh sankhya rekha wala kaam khatam hote hi {aside} ki baat zaroor karenge.
asidePark.en: Once we finish this number line, we will surely talk about {aside}.

asidePark.hi: {aside} ki baat bhi hogi, bas yeh sankhya rekha wala kaam khatam ho jaaye.
asidePark.en: We'll talk about {aside} too, right after this number line.

asidePark.hi: Wah, {aside} ki baat sambhaal ke rakhi hai, baad mein zaroor sunungi.
asidePark.en: Oh, I've kept the {aside} bit safe, and I'll surely hear it later.

asideReturn.hi: {aside} mein tumhe sabse mazedaar kya lagta hai?
asideReturn.en: What's the most fun part of {aside} for you?

asideReturn.hi: Chalo, {aside} ke baare mein batao, tumhe woh kyun pasand hai?
asideReturn.en: Okay, tell me about {aside}: why do you like it?

asideReturn.hi: {aside} wali baat batao na, tumhe uski kaunsi baat pasand hai?
asideReturn.en: Tell me about {aside}: what do you like about it?

hindiSwitch.hi: Achha, yeh baat Hindi mein kehti hoon.
hindiSwitch.en: Okay, let me put this in Hindi.

hindiSwitch.hi: Bilkul, ab yeh Hindi mein bolti hoon.
hindiSwitch.en: Of course, I'll say this in Hindi now.

hindiSwitch.hi: Theek hai, main yeh Hindi mein bolti hoon.
hindiSwitch.en: Sure, I'll say it in Hindi.

askAgain.hi: Ek baar aur bolo, main sun rahi hoon.
askAgain.en: Say it once more, I'm listening.

backTo.hi: Ab us sawaal par lautte hain jo humne pehle chhoda tha.
backTo.en: Now let's return to the question we left earlier.

backTo.hi: Theek hai, ab wapas usi sawaal par chalte hain.
backTo.en: Alright, let's go back to that question now.

backTo.hi: Chalo, ab pichhle sawaal par wapas chalte hain.
backTo.en: Okay, let's go back to the earlier question.

hook.convey: one whole stretch from start = 0 to finish = 1; stopping exactly halfway → standing on a real spot → 0 and 1 have no name for it → fractions are numbers that live between 0 and 1

use.hi: Cricket ki pitch socho. Ek stump 0 par, doosra 1 par. Batsman run lene bhaaga aur theek beech mein ruk gaya. Woh pitch ki ek pakki jagah par khada hai, toh us jagah ka bhi ek number hai.
use.en: Picture a cricket pitch. One stump at 0, the other at 1. The batsman sets off for a run and stops right in the middle. He's standing on a real spot, so that spot has a number too.

use.hi: Ghar 0 par, school 1 km par. School bus aadhe raaste mein ruk gayi. Na 0 par, na 1 par, beech mein kahin. Us jagah ka bhi number hota hai.
use.en: Home is at 0, school at 1 km. The school bus stops halfway. Not at 0, not at 1, somewhere in between. That place has a number too.

use.hi: Game mein level ka bar 0 se bharna shuru hota hai, aur 1 par level khatam. Abhi bar aadha bhara hai. Matlab woh 0 aur 1 ke beech ke ek number par ruka hai.
use.en: In a game the level bar starts filling at 0, and at 1 the level is done. Right now it's half full. So it has stopped at a number between 0 and 1.

explain.convey: 0 and 1 at the ends; one cut exactly in the middle → 2 equal gaps; the middle mark = 1/2 → 1/2 is a number with its own place, between 0 and 1, not at 2

point.hi: Yeh rahi 0 se 1 tak ki line. Upar theek beech mein ek mark hai, toh upar line ke 2 barabar gaps ban gaye. Is mark ka naam hai 1/2.
point.en: Here's a line from 0 to 1. On top, one mark right in the middle, and now the top of the line has 2 equal gaps. This mark is called 1/2.

prompt.hi: {friend} ka kehna hai ki 1/3 toh 3 ke paas aata hai. Tumhe kya lagta hai: 1/3 isi 0 se 1 wali line par hai, ya 3 ke paas?
prompt.en: {friend} says 1/3 goes near 3. What do you think: is 1/3 on this line from 0 to 1, or near 3?

simpler.hi: 1/3 ka neeche wala number 3 dekho: woh batata hai 0 se 1 ko kitne barabar gaps mein kaatna hai. 1/3 bhi ek poore ka ek tukda hai.
simpler.en: Look at the bottom number of 1/3, the 3: it says how many equal gaps to cut 0 to 1 into. 1/3 is also a piece of one whole.

why.hi: neeche ka 3 matlab 0 se 1 ke 3 barabar gaps, aur pehla gap isi line par khatam hota hai
why.en: the bottom 3 means 3 equal gaps from 0 to 1, and the first gap ends right on this line

simpler.hi: Line ke theek beech mein ek mark hai. Woh line ko do barabar gaps mein baant-ta hai, isliye uska naam 1/2 hai.
simpler.en: There is a mark right in the middle of the line. It splits the line into two equal gaps, so its name is 1/2.

explain.convey: same 0 to 1, now 6 marks inside → 7 equal gaps (gaps = marks inside + 1); bottom number = number of equal gaps in 0 to 1; first mark from 0 = end of 1 gap = 1/7; the name comes from gaps, not marks

point.hi: Wahi 0 se 1 ki line, par ab upar 6 marks hain. Marks mat gino, gaps gino: 7 barabar gaps. Toh 0 ke baad pehla mark hai 1/7.
point.en: Same line from 0 to 1, but now there are 6 marks on top. Don't count the marks, count the gaps: 7 equal gaps. So the first mark after 0 is 1/7.

prompt.hi: Ab line ke neeche dekho. Wahan 0 aur 1 ke beech 7 marks hain, sab barabar doori par. Neeche line kitne barabar gaps mein bati hai?
prompt.en: Now look under the line. There are 7 marks between 0 and 1, all evenly spaced. How many equal gaps does that make below?

why.hi: beech ke marks se gaps hamesha ek zyada, toh 7 marks ke 8 gaps
why.en: there's always one more gap than marks in between, so 7 marks make 8 gaps

simpler.hi: Upar 6 marks the aur gaps 7, yaani gaps ek zyada. Neeche ke 7 marks par bhi yahi chalega.
simpler.en: On top there were 6 marks and 7 gaps, one more gap. The same works for the 7 marks below.

explain.convey: the same 0 to 1 in 8 equal gaps → more gaps than the 7 before → each gap smaller; 1/8 = first mark, right next to 0; 1/2 still the middle mark (4 of the 8 gaps); more equal gaps in the same whole → each gap shorter → 1/8 sits closer to 0 than 1/7 and 1/2

point.hi: Ab wahi 0 se 1, par upar 8 barabar gaps hain. 7 gaps se zyada gaps, toh har ek chhota gap hai. Pehla mark 1/8, bilkul 0 se chipka hua.
point.en: Now the same 0 to 1, but on top there are 8 equal gaps. More gaps than 7, so each one is a smaller gap. The first mark is 1/8, right up against 0.

prompt.hi: Ab neeche dekho: wahi line 10 barabar gaps mein kati hai. 0 ke zyada paas kaun rukega: 1/8 ya 1/10?
prompt.en: Now look below: the same line cut into 10 equal gaps. Which stops closer to 0: 1/8 or 1/10?

why.hi: 10 gaps wala har gap 8 gaps wale se chhota hai, isliye 1/10 pehle ruk jaata hai, 0 ke paas
why.en: a gap out of 10 is smaller than a gap out of 8, so 1/10 stops sooner, nearer 0

simpler.hi: 8 gaps hue toh pehla mark 1/8 ekdum 0 ke paas aa gaya. Gaps jitne zyada, pehla mark 0 ke utna hi paas.
simpler.en: With 8 gaps, the first mark, 1/8, moved right up to 0. The more gaps, the closer the first mark sits to 0.

problem.hi: Ghar 0 par hai aur school 1 km par. Beech raaste mein 3 bijli ke khambe barabar doori par khade hain. Pehla khamba ghar se kitne km door hai?
problem.en: Home is at 0 and school is at 1 km. Along the road between them stand 3 electric poles, evenly spaced. How many km from home is the first pole?

simpler.hi: Ghar se school tak 1 km ka raasta hai, aur beech mein 3 khambe barabar doori par hain. Pehla khamba kahan hai, yeh dhoondhna hai.
simpler.en: The road from home to school is 1 km, with 3 poles evenly spaced between. We need where the first pole stands.

givens.hi: poora raasta 1 km ka, aur beech mein 3 khambe
givens.en: a 1 km road with 3 poles in between

find.hi: pehle khambe ki doori, km mein
find.en: how far the first pole is, in km

do.hi: Ek line kheencho, ghar 0 par aur school 1 par
do.en: Draw a line with home at 0 and school at 1

why.hi: ghar se school tak ka poora raasta hi humara ek poora hai
why.en: the whole road from home to school is our one whole

simpler.hi: Bas do jagah pakki karo: ghar 0 par, school 1 par. Beech ka saara raasta ek poora hai.
simpler.en: Fix just two spots: home at 0, school at 1. All the road in between is one whole.

do.hi: Khambe mat gino, unke beech ke gaps gino
do.en: Don't count the poles, count the gaps between them

why.hi: beech mein jitne marks hon, gaps hamesha usse ek zyada
why.en: there is always one more gap than marks in between

simpler.hi: Ghar se pehle khambe tak ek gap, phir khambe se khamba, aur aakhri khambe se school tak ek. 3 khambe, 4 gaps.
simpler.en: Home to the first pole is one gap, then pole to pole, then the last pole to school. 3 poles, 4 gaps.

prompt.hi: Raasta 4 barabar gaps mein bata hai, aur pehla khamba ghar se bas ek gap door hai. Woh kitne km par hai?
prompt.en: The road is in 4 equal gaps, and the first pole is just one gap from home. At how many km is it?

why.hi: raasta 4 barabar gaps mein bata hai aur pehla khamba theek ek gap par hai
why.en: the road is in 4 equal gaps and the first pole stands exactly one gap along

simpler.hi: Poora 1 km, 4 barabar tukde. Ek tukda poore ka kaunsa hissa hai, bas yahi socho.
simpler.en: The whole 1 km, in 4 equal pieces. Just think which part of the whole one piece is.

answer.hi: pehla khamba ghar se 1/4 km door hai
answer.en: the first pole is 1/4 km from home

why.hi: 4 barabar gaps mein har gap 1/4 km ka hai, aur pehla khamba 0 se theek ek gap par khada hai
why.en: with 4 equal gaps each gap is 1/4 km, and the first pole stands exactly one gap from 0

prompt.hi: Is line par 0 aur 1 ke beech 10 marks hain, barabar doori par. 0 ke baad pehla mark kaunsa fraction hai?
prompt.en: This line has 10 evenly spaced marks between 0 and 1. What fraction is the first mark after 0?

why.hi: 10 marks se line ke 11 barabar gaps bante hain, aur pehla mark ek gap par hai, yaani 1/11
why.en: 10 marks make 11 equal gaps, and the first mark is one gap along, at 1/11

simpler.hi: Marks chhodo, gaps gino. 0 se 1 ki line par 10 marks se jitne gaps bane, wahi neeche wala number hai.
simpler.en: Forget the marks, count the gaps. On a line from 0 to 1, however many gaps the 10 marks make, that's the bottom number.

prompt.hi: {friend} kehta hai 1/11 line par 1/4 ke baad aata hai, kyunki 11, 4 se bada hai. {friend} sahi hai ya galat?
prompt.en: {friend} says 1/11 comes after 1/4 on the line, because 11 is bigger than 4. Is {friend} right or wrong?

why.hi: wahi poora 11 mein bata toh har gap chhota, isliye 1/11 pehle rukta hai, 1/4 se pehle; {friend} galat hai
why.en: the same whole cut into 11 makes each gap smaller, so 1/11 stops sooner, before 1/4; {friend} is wrong

simpler.hi: Socho ek roti 4 logon mein bati, ya 11 logon mein. Jis baar tukda chhota mile, woh line par pehle rukta hai.
simpler.en: Imagine one roti shared among 4, or among 11. Whichever way the piece is smaller stops earlier on the line.

prompt.hi: Line 0 se 1 tak 9 barabar gaps mein hai. Ek khilona chalkar pehle mark par ruka. {friend} kehta hai woh kisi number par nahi khada. Woh kis number par khada hai?
prompt.en: The line from 0 to 1 is in 9 equal gaps. A toy walks along and stops at the first mark. {friend} says it is not standing on any number. What number is it on?

why.hi: line ke 9 barabar gaps hain, aur pehla mark 0 se ek gap par: ek pakki jagah, ek number, 1/9
why.en: the line has 9 equal gaps, and the first mark is one gap from 0: one real spot, one number, 1/9

simpler.hi: Khilona hawa mein nahi, line ki ek jagah par khada hai. 0 se 1 tak kitne barabar gaps hain, aur woh kitne gap chala, yeh dekho.
simpler.en: The toy is not in the air; it stands on one spot of the line. See how many equal gaps run from 0 to 1, and how many gaps it walked.

ladder.why: den 2: one cut, gaps obvious → fraction as a place on the road; same den as e1
den 4 (halves halved, as in e2 and the worked example) → 2nd mark = 2/4 → same spot as 1/2; gap-value thinking, not mark counting
den 5 given only as marks (4 inside) → must convert marks to gaps; error-spot on the count-marks trap
den 6 again but given as 5 inside marks → contrasts with rl-o1 (same den, gaps given) → explain why the label is wrong

remediation.move: ribbon at a tailor's shop, 0 to 1 m, one line cut in 7 on top and 12 below; marks = chalk marks (nishaan), gaps = ribbon pieces; marks inside + 1 = pieces; a mark's name comes from counting pieces, not marks; top: 6 marks → 7 pieces → first mark at 1/7 m; then below: 11 marks → 12 pieces → 1/12 m (the trap says 1/11)

say.hi: Darzi ka ribbon socho, 0 se 1 metre. Upar 6 chalk ke nishaan hain, aur ribbon ke 7 barabar tukde. Pehla nishaan pehle tukde ke end par hai, isliye uska naam 1/7 metre. Naam tukde ginkar milta hai, nishaan ginkar nahi.
say.en: Picture a tailor's ribbon, 0 to 1 metre. On top there are 6 chalk marks, and the ribbon is in 7 equal pieces. The first mark ends the first piece, so its name is 1/7 metre. The name comes from counting pieces, not marks.

simpler.hi: 6 nishaan, 7 tukde. Tukde gino, toh pehla nishaan 1/7 metre par hai.
simpler.en: 6 marks, 7 pieces. Count the pieces, and the first mark is at 1/7 metre.

prompt.hi: Ribbon ki neeche wali line par 11 nishaan hain, barabar doori par. Pehla nishaan kitne metre par hai?
prompt.en: On the ribbon's lower line there are 11 evenly spaced marks. At how many metres is the first mark?

why.hi: 11 nishaan se ribbon ke 12 barabar tukde bante hain, aur pehla nishaan pehle tukde ke end par, 1/12 metre par
why.en: 11 marks cut the ribbon into 12 equal pieces, and the first mark ends the first piece, at 1/12 metre

simpler.hi: Nishaan nahi, tukde gino. Tukde hamesha nishaanon se ek zyada hote hain.
simpler.en: Count the pieces, not the marks. There's always one more piece than marks.

remediation.move: on the then-card's own board (one 0-to-1 line, fifths on top, sixths below, 1/5 marked), naming none of its numbers: both rows are the same whole; a bigger bottom number shares the same whole into more pieces, so each piece is smaller → bigger bottom number = smaller piece; then the child places 1/6: between 0 and 1/5, not after it

say.hi: Upar aur neeche, dono ek hi line hain, 0 se 1 tak: wahi ek poora. Fraction ka neeche wala number jitna bada, wahi poora utne zyada tukdon mein bata, aur har tukda utna chhota. Bada number matlab bada tukda nahi.
say.en: Top and bottom are the same line, 0 to 1: the same one whole. The bigger a fraction's bottom number, the more pieces that same whole is shared into, and the smaller each piece. A bigger number does not mean a bigger piece.

simpler.hi: Ek hi poora, zyada tukde, toh har tukda chhota. Fraction ka neeche wala number bada ho, toh uska tukda chhota.
simpler.en: One whole, more pieces, so each piece is smaller. When a fraction's bottom number is bigger, its piece is smaller.

prompt.hi: Upar pehla mark 1/5 hai, neeche line 6 barabar tukdon mein. 1/6 kahaan aayega: 0 aur 1/5 ke beech, ya 1/5 ke baad?
prompt.en: On top the first mark is 1/5; below, the line is in 6 equal pieces. Where does 1/6 go: between 0 and 1/5, or after 1/5?

why.hi: 6 tukdon wala har tukda 5 tukdon wale se chhota hai, isliye 1/6, 0 aur 1/5 ke beech rukta hai
why.en: a piece out of 6 is smaller than a piece out of 5, so 1/6 stops between 0 and 1/5

simpler.hi: 1/6 wala tukda 1/5 wale tukde se chhota hai. Chhota tukda pehle ruk jaata hai.
simpler.en: A 1/6 piece is smaller than a 1/5 piece. A smaller piece stops sooner.

remediation.move: road from home (0) to the chai stall (1 km), one line in 7 equal stretches on top; a toy walks from home and stops at the first mark → it stands on one real spot of the road → that spot has a number, 1/7 km; then the same road in 6 stretches below: the toy stops at the fifth mark after 0 → that spot is a number too, 5/6 km (the trap says 5 and 6)

say.hi: Ghar se chai ki dukaan tak sadak hai, 0 se 1 km. Upar woh 7 barabar hisson mein hai. Khilona chala aur pehle mark par ruk gaya. Woh sadak ki ek pakki jagah par khada hai, aur us jagah ka number hai 1/7 km.
say.en: There's a road from home to the chai stall, 0 to 1 km. On top it's in 7 equal stretches. A toy walks and stops at the first mark. It's standing on a real spot of the road, and that spot's number is 1/7 km.

simpler.hi: Khilona hawa mein nahi, sadak ki ek pakki jagah par khada hai. Us jagah ka bhi number hai, 1/7 km.
simpler.en: The toy isn't floating; it stands on one real spot of the road. That spot has a number too, 1/7 km.

prompt.hi: Neeche wahi sadak 6 barabar hisson mein hai. Khilona neeche 0 ke baad paanchve mark par ruka. Woh kis number par hai?
prompt.en: Below, the same road is in 6 equal stretches. The toy stops at the fifth mark after 0 below. What number is it on?

why.hi: neeche sadak 6 barabar hisson mein hai, aur paanchva mark 0 se paanch kadam par hai: ek pakki jagah, 5/6 km
why.en: the lower road is in 6 equal stretches and the fifth mark is five steps from 0: one real spot, 5/6 km

simpler.hi: Neeche bhi wahi sadak hai, 6 barabar hisson mein. 0 se paanchve mark tak kitne hisse hain, gino.
simpler.en: The line below is the same road, in 6 equal stretches. Count the stretches from 0 to the fifth mark.

bridgeToNext.hi: Abhi tak hum 0 se sirf ek hop chale. Ab ek se zyada hop chalenge, aur upar ka number batayega kitne.
bridgeToNext.en: So far we've taken just one hop from 0. Now we'll take more than one, and the top number will tell us how many.

simpler.hi: Ab tak 0 se ek hop chale. Ab upar ka number batayega kitne hop chalne hain.
simpler.en: So far we took one hop from 0. Now the top number tells us how many hops to take.

hook.convey: same 0-to-1 stretch cut into equal stretches; the stop is not the first mark but several stretches on → its name needs two facts: how many equal stretches make the whole (bottom), how many are covered from 0 (top)

use.hi: Cricket pitch ko 4 barabar hisson mein baanto. Batsman 0 wale stump se bhaaga aur 3 hisse paar karke ruka. Uski jagah batane ke liye do cheezein chahiye: pitch ke kitne hisse hain, aur usne kitne paar kiye.
use.en: Split a cricket pitch into 4 equal parts. The batsman runs from the stump at 0 and stops after 3 parts. To name his spot we need two things: how many parts the pitch has, and how many he crossed.

use.hi: Game ka loading bar 0 se 1 tak hai, 5 barabar khaanon mein. Abhi 2 khaane bhare hain. Kitna bhara, yeh batane ke liye do number chahiye, neeche wala aur upar wala.
use.en: A game's loading bar runs from 0 to 1, in 5 equal boxes. Right now 2 boxes are full. To say how full it is, we need two numbers, a bottom one and a top one.

explain.convey: thirds: bottom 3 → 0 to 1 in 3 equal gaps; top 2 → 2 hops of 1/3 from 0; landing mark = 2/3 → one point, one number, not 2 and 3 separately

point.hi: Is baar upar line 3 barabar gaps mein kati hai, har gap 1/3. 0 se 2 hop lagao, ek, do, aur hum 2/3 par aa gaye. 2/3 ek hi jagah hai, ek hi number.
point.en: This time, on top, the line is cut into 3 equal gaps, each gap 1/3. Take 2 hops from 0, one, two, and we're at 2/3. 2/3 is one place, one number.

prompt.hi: Neeche wali line 8 barabar gaps mein kati hai. 0 se 5 hop lo. Kis fraction par pahunche?
prompt.en: The lower line is cut into 8 equal gaps. Take 5 hops from 0. Which fraction do you land on?

why.hi: har hop 1/8 ka, aur aise 5 hop mile toh 5/8
why.en: each hop is 1/8, and 5 of them make 5/8

simpler.hi: Fraction ka neeche wala number batata hai ek poore ke kitne barabar gaps, upar wala batata hai kitne hop. Pehle neeche wali line ke gaps gino, phir hop.
simpler.en: A fraction's bottom number says how many equal gaps one whole has, its top says how many hops. First count the gaps on the lower line, then the hops.

explain.convey: still thirds: 3 hops of 1/3 → every gap used → land exactly on 1 → 3/3 = 1; top < bottom → stop before 1; top = bottom → reach 1

mustSay.hi: upar wala number aur neeche wala number barabar
mustSay.en: top number and bottom number are equal

point.hi: Upar ki line 3 barabar gaps mein bati hai. 0 se teen gap chalo toh theek 1 aata hai, isliye wahan 3/3 = 1. Jab fraction ka upar wala number aur neeche wala number barabar ho, chalna theek 1 par khatam hota hai.
point.en: The top line is cut into 3 equal gaps. Walk three gaps from 0 and you land exactly on 1, so there 3/3 = 1. When a fraction's top number and bottom number are equal, the walk ends exactly on 1.

prompt.hi: Neeche wali line par har hop 1/5 ka hai. 0 se chalkar theek 1 par utarne ke liye kitne hop chahiye?
prompt.en: On the lower line each hop is 1/5. How many hops from 0 to land exactly on 1?

why.hi: 1/5 ke 5 hop milkar 5/5 banate hain, aur 5/5 = 1
why.en: 5 hops of 1/5 make 5/5, and 5/5 = 1

simpler.hi: Teen gap chalkar 1 aaya, kyunki 3/3 = 1. Ab 1/5 wale hop mein bhi fraction ka upar wala number neeche wale ke barabar lao.
simpler.en: Three gaps reached 1, because 3/3 = 1. With 1/5 hops too, make the fraction's top number match its bottom number.

explain.convey: each third cut in 2 → 6 equal gaps; the middle = half of the 6 gaps = 3 gaps → 3/6 = 1/2; fewer than half the gaps (2/6) → before the middle; more than half (5/6) → after the middle

point.hi: Ab line ke 6 barabar gaps hain. Theek beech ka mark 3/6 hai, aur 3, 6 ka aadha hai, toh 3/6 = 1/2. 2/6 beech se pehle aata hai, 5/6 beech ke baad.
point.en: Now the line has 6 equal gaps. The mark right in the middle is 3/6, and 3 is half of 6, so 3/6 = 1/2. 2/6 comes before the middle, 5/6 after it.

prompt.hi: Isi line par 4/6 kahaan aayega: beech se pehle, ya beech ke baad?
prompt.en: On this same line, where does 4/6 go: before the middle, or after it?

why.hi: beech 3/6 par hai, aur upar ka 4 usse ek zyada, toh ek gap aage, beech ke baad
why.en: the middle is at 3/6, and a top of 4 is one more, so one gap on, after the middle

simpler.hi: Beech 3/6 par hai. Upar ka number 3 se chhota ho toh pehle, bada ho toh baad.
simpler.en: The middle is at 3/6. A top number below 3 comes before it, above 3 comes after.

problem.hi: Ek number line 0 se 1 tak hai. Is par 2/5 ka mark dhoondo.
problem.en: A number line runs from 0 to 1. Find the mark for 2/5.

simpler.hi: 0 se 1 ki ek rekha hai, aur us par 2/5 dikhana hai. Neeche ka 5 aur upar ka 2, dono kaam aayenge.
simpler.en: There is a line from 0 to 1, and we show 2/5 on it. The bottom 5 and the top 2 both help.

givens.en: 2/5 has 5 on the bottom and 2 on top

do.hi: Neeche ka 5 dekho, aur 0 se 1 ko 5 barabar gaps mein kaato
do.en: Read the bottom 5 and cut 0 to 1 into 5 equal gaps

why.hi: neeche wala number hi poore ke gaps ginta hai
why.en: the bottom number is the count of gaps in the whole

simpler.hi: 2/5 ka neeche wala 5 hai. Toh line ke 5 barabar tukde karo, beech mein 4 marks aayenge.
simpler.en: The bottom of 2/5 is 5. So cut the line into 5 equal pieces; 4 marks land in between.

do.hi: Ab dekho ek gap kitne ka hai
do.en: Now see what one gap is worth

why.hi: 5 barabar gaps milke 1 poora banate hain
why.en: 5 equal gaps together make 1 whole

simpler.hi: Paanch gaps, aur sab milke ek poora. Toh ek gap poore ka 1/5 hai.
simpler.en: Five gaps make one whole together. So one gap is 1/5 of the whole.

prompt.hi: Ab upar wala number. 0 se utne gap aage chalo. 0 ke baad kaunse mark par ruke?
prompt.en: Now the top number. Move that many gaps on from 0. Which mark after 0 do you stop at?

why.hi: upar ka 2 kehta hai 1/5 ke do gap chalo, isliye hum doosre mark par rukte hain
why.en: the top 2 says take two gaps of 1/5, so we stop at the second mark

simpler.hi: 2/5 ka upar wala 2 hai. 0 se ek-ek gap karke chalo, aur gino.
simpler.en: The top of 2/5 is 2. Step from 0 one gap at a time, and count.

why.hi: upar ka 2 kehta hai 0 se 1/5 ke 2 gap chalo
why.en: the top 2 says move 2 gaps of 1/5 from 0

prompt.hi: 0 aur 1 ke beech 5 marks hain, sab barabar doori par. 0 ke baad chautha mark kaunsa fraction hai?
